title: Laying the Groundwork for the Future
text: “Well then, wouldn’t it all be settled if Naofumi just apologized right here and now?!”
Itsuki is just so annoying. He’s acting all righteous while spouting complete nonsense. But… even this pig can come up with a quick excuse on the spot.
He can’t demand money, and he can’t even use the letter of introduction as an excuse. In the end, the king didn’t give his permission. But… this excuse has practically no effect on Ren.
“Motoyasu, Naofumi. Something’s off about this country… It’s almost as if the king, the princess… the entire country is acting to persecute Naofumi, isn’t it?”
“Boo-boo! Boo-boo-boo-boo!”
The pig is making excuses to Ren, but it seems Ren isn’t listening anymore. I could tell him the truth right now, but that would create a discrepancy with the future.
“I-I guess so…?”
“It’s all because Naofumi-san won’t reflect on his actions! Come on! Bow your head!”
“Why the hell do I have to apologize to Itsuki?! Even if I were to apologize, it wouldn’t be to you!”
My father spat out the words with obvious displeasure. That’s enough. Perhaps my father understands this as well, for he turns his back on the hourglass while dramatically displaying his anger.
“It’s fine. It’s not like we have to do it right now anyway… Come on, Motoyasu, let’s go.”
“Understood.”
“…Hmph. Itsuki, I think you should be a little more skeptical.”

As we followed my father out, Ren and his companions also left the building, taking care not to make eye contact with Itsuki. After we left the building, Buta called out to Ren, so Ren very reluctantly went back inside. Most likely, they were planning to take advantage of the fact that my Father and I had left to give the sand from the hourglass to Buta as material for weapons.
After all, various materials were occasionally provided under the guise of aid from the government. If we placed an order, they’d make us reasonably good equipment. But that’s all in the past now.
“She was a pretty rude girl, wasn’t she?”
“Yeah, I was torn about whether to just cut her loose.”
“Keel, Sakura, please stop that—it’ll cause a commotion.”
“But big brother…”
Keel looked at his Father with a frustrated expression. Father smiled gently, as if trying to reason with him, and began to speak.
“Shh, this is a secret, so you mustn’t tell anyone.”
“Why not?”
“Hmm… Maybe because I’m a bad person myself. Do you think Ren will believe me?”
“From what I can tell, he’s already brimming with suspicion toward the kingdom. At that rate, I think he’ll figure it out sooner or later.”
“I hope so. That said… if we don’t keep it in check, our knowledge of the future won’t be of any use, so let’s leave it at that.”
“Got it.”
I’m glad Ren is suspicious, but if that turns into an unpredictable factor, it’ll actually cause us trouble. As Father said, this is probably the safest approach.
“Well, now that we’re done with our business, let’s get a good night’s sleep by the waves and prepare for tomorrow.”
“Yay! Big bro! Cook us some food to get ready for tomorrow!”
“Okay, okay. I’ll cook for you guys down by the riverbank over in the grasslands.”
“Yesss!”
“Sakura’s looking forward to it, too.”
“I’m looking forward to it as well.”
“Naofumi-sama, I’d like to request some refined cuisine.”
“……I’ll have a little chat with Motoyasu and Yuki later, okay?”
After that, while Father was cooking by the river and Sakura and the others were enjoying their meal, Yuki and I ended up getting lectured by him.

He went on and on about how he wasn’t the type to be pushed down—if anything, he was the one doing the pushing—and that romantic relationships should only be built with mutual consent. Thinking back on my future Father… I get the feeling he was somewhat dominated by my Big Sister—or am I mistaken?
It just came to me. It was Big Sister who encouraged my Father to give me and Filo-tan permission to go on a date.
And so, that day passed by in a heartwarming manner.
The next day. The time for the waves is drawing near.
“I’ve brought plenty of medicine, and we’ve gone over everything many times just to be safe. I’ve done everything I can to prepare… but I still can’t seem to shake this anxiety.”
Father muttered as he fiddled with his gear bag.
“You’re such a worrier, big bro. Back then, I just ran away from the waves, but we’ll be fine now!”
Keel gave my Father a few gentle pats with his paw to encourage him.
“Sakura will do her best, too.”

Sakura-chan said this after practicing repeatedly to ensure she could draw the sword at her waist at a moment’s notice. Now, how about me? Well, I’ve already experienced the Melromarc Wave once, after all. I’m not particularly nervous.

Back then, I charged headlong toward the wave’s fissure, full of enthusiasm at finally being able to take on the wave. I was fighting the chimera with a bit too much excitement, wasn’t I? I think my Father was directing the evacuation. Considering the warnings I received during the next wave, it’s certainly important to get non-combatants to safety.

I’d fire a flare to signal that reinforcements from the castle were on their way, then charge like a wild boar. It was truly a headlong rush. What should I do this time? Quelling the wave immediately is one option, but…
“Father, what should we do this time? If we wanted to, we could quell this wave instantly.”
“Hmm… but if it becomes obvious just how strong Motoyasu-kun is, there’s a high chance that his knowledge of the future will become useless, isn’t there?”
“That’s true. Then let’s hold back a bit. After all, Ren and Itsuki can handle this wave with ease. We’ll win even if we just stand by and do nothing.”
“Well... that’s true, but abandoning a life that could be saved just to avoid getting caught up in a conspiracy... I feel like that’s wrong, too.”
How kind of you. Motoyasu, I can’t stop crying at Father’s compassion.
“Did I say something weird? Motoyasu-kun is crying while saluting.”
“Oink…”
“Huh? I told you I’m a weirdo, so I wouldn’t know… Elena, show a little enthusiasm, will you?”
“Oink.”
“It’s not like I’m putting you in charge, Elena. I’m just saying we should try our best to keep casualties to a minimum—just enough so we don’t draw too much attention.”
“Boo.”
“It’s a hassle, but… you know? This is the key to victory, so let’s show some enthusiasm.”
“Boo.”
The Lazy Pig shrugged slightly before nodding. Is that a sign of motivation or a lack thereof? Well, I wasn’t expecting much from a Lazy Pig to begin with.
“Lord Motoyasu, what should Kou and I do?”
“Just follow my Father’s instructions.”
“Understood.”
As long as we follow Father’s orders, everything will go smoothly. It’s been proven in the first world. With his brilliant leadership alone, our future is secure.

“For now… according to Motoyasu-kun, we’re supposed to teleport to Riyute Village, so let’s prioritize evacuating the residents. Motoyasu-kun, you help out too—that way, we should at least be able to minimize casualties.”
“That’s the same strategy as in the future, isn’t it?”

“Yeah. But since Motoyasu-kun’s original slot will be open, once the evacuation is complete, he should head toward the Wave Boss. Please try to hide your true power as much as possible. Yuki-chan and Kou, you two should keep that in mind, too.”
“Got it!”
“Understood.”
We nodded in agreement to Father’s orders. We used to charge headlong into things, but this time we’re saving many lives. Thinking about that gives me a real boost of energy.
“Kou’s gonna do his best! Are wave monsters tasty?”
“I don’t know about that…? I’d like to get the Wave Boss’s materials, though. I hear they’re pretty good.”
“After we defeated it, we stripped off some of the materials and left the rest behind. Since Father had a shield that looked like it could handle it, I think he took care of cleaning it up.”
“Well, since I don’t think Itsuki or Ren are paying attention to that, let’s take it for ourselves. It looks pretty big to carry anyway… though finding a place to store it might be a problem.”
“So you’re going to give the boss’s materials to my dad, huh?”
“Oh, that’s a good idea. I bet he can turn the bones and other parts into weapons and armor… even though I’m completely broke.”
“The day after the Wave, Trash gave us some aid money, calling it a ‘severance payment.’”

My father is frowning, looking extremely displeased. Well, calling it a “severance payment” is basically a sign that they’re kicking him out. To kick out my father—who’s far stronger than Ren or Itsuki—is truly the act of a foolish king. I’m already looking forward to seeing how we’ll deal with that foolish king.
“Well, after the next Wave, I think the Queen will return and provide my father with the aid he’s owed, so we’ll just have to be patient.”
“I know that. Yeah, at least we’ll get some financial aid. Besides, we’re not exactly short on money over in Siltvelt anyway.”
“By the time the second wave hits, we’ll be on the wanted list anyway, so we won’t have to hold back. Just a little more patience.”
“Yeah. I’ll just put up with it by thinking of the king and Bitch as pitiful people.”
“That’s the right attitude. Well then, the wave is almost upon us.”

I think back to my future Father. Back when I, a mere clown, was berating my Father… I wonder what he was thinking as he faced that first wave. I can understand how he must have resented the whole world. When I was betrayed by the Crimson Swine… I felt the same way.
Filo-tan… where are you? Thanks to you, I didn’t end up hating the world. It’s because you were there that I’m able to love the world.
I don’t think there was anyone there to help Father at that moment. Was Big Sister there to support him? Am I able to support Father? Big Sister.

…Come to think of it, where exactly did you join us? At this rate, I won’t be able to meet you. I’m pretty sure you’d been reduced to slavery… but I’m not entirely sure. I didn’t see you when I bought the Keel, did I?

Hmm. Well, I’m sure she’s living happily somewhere. I can’t imagine that strong, dignified, and healthy Big Sister of mine would be brought down by just anything. I’m sure she’s living a vibrant life.
Around the time the turmoil in Melromarc ended, my Father tried to rebuild the village. We should look for her then. I’ll just have to support my Father for Big Sister’s sake.
“It’s about time.”
The numbers on the hourglass in my field of vision are approaching zero.
“Let’s do our best to minimize casualties as much as possible. Overcoming this wave will lay the groundwork for the future.”
“Let’s do this, big bro! This time, I’ll protect everyone—even for the ones I couldn’t protect before!”
“Sakura will do her best.”
“I’ll protect Yuki, too.”
“Kou’s going off to play with monsters—”
“Oink… oink oink.”
The Lazy Pig grunted in a low-key tone, as if saying, “Ah… yeah, yeah.”
“Alright, Motoyasu-kun. Give everyone a pep talk.”
“Understood. Everyone has worked hard to get stronger for today. To achieve even better results than the future I know… let’s do our best!”
As I gave the signal, the number hit zero, and the first wave of this loop began.
